newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-TILLEKERATNE CENTURY UPSTAGED BY IJAZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TILLEKERATNE CENTURY UPSTAGED BY IJAZ.

text.p: Middle-order batsman Hashan Tillekeratne completed his sixth test century on Sunday as Sri Lanka were bowled out shortly after lunch for 330 by Pakistan on the second day of the opening test.
However, he had to yield centre stage to Pakistan's number three batsman Ijaz Ahmed who struck 90 not out as the Pakistanis replied boldly to reach 200 for two at the close.

With opener Salim Elahi being bowled by Chaminda Vaas for nought, Ijaz marched to the crease to hit 10 fours as he shared partnerships of 102 for the second wicket with Rameez Raja, who made 50, and 98 unbroken for the third with former captain Salim Malik (47 not out).
Rameez completed his 22nd test half-century in two hours but then clipped an easy catch to Arjuna Ranatunga at short midwicket off the brisk off-spin of Kumar Dharmasena.

Ijaz, driving fluently on both sides of the wicket, completed his first 50 in 156 minutues off 114 balls with six fours while Malik offered solid support at the opposite end. Towards the end of the day both batsmen began to plunder a tiring attack.

Earlier, Sri Lanka, resuming on their overnight score of 254 for five, added 76 as they lost their last five wickets, four of them going to off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq who claimed his first five-wicket haul in test cricket.
Romesh Kaluwitharana scored the two runs he needed to complete his fourth test half-century but he was out shortly after when he attempted a big hit off Saqlain and was bowled for 57.
He hit eight fours in a stay of 106 minutes and his dismissal ended an 89-run partnership with Tillekeratne for the sixth wicket.
Tillekeratne, who was 65 not out overnight, was given a life on 85 when Mushtaq Ahmed spilled a chance at mid-off and he duly completed his hundred in 325 minutes off 215 balls.
However, the left-hander could not get going after lunch and when he attempted to cut Saqlain, he could only edge a simple catch to Asif Mujtaba at slip.
Saqlain also took the wickets of Dharmasena and Nuwan Zoysa to finish with his best test figures of five for 89.
